problem: The sentence 'a single-player game has neither' (persistence nor shared state) clashes with the chapter's own definition of persistence: a single-player game does keep its world state after you quit, through a save file. Read literally, the trap is wrong; only shared, cross-user persistence is missing.
fix: Say: 'A metaverse needs persistence and shared state across users and devices; a single-player game keeps state only on your own device and has no shared state with other users.'

problem: Only ttotal is stated to be in ms. The other three terms are added to it, so a student can lose marks by mixing seconds and milliseconds in the exam.
fix: Define all four terms in the same unit: 'ttotal, trender, tnetwork and tscan are all in ms; tnetwork counts the full round trip (uplink plus downlink).'

problem: Each step is numbered twice ('step 1: 1.'), which reads as a formatting slip in an otherwise clean solution.
fix: Use one numbering only: 'Step 1: Network budget = 20 − 8 − 4 = 8 ms.'
